html:
The White Revolution was a set of reforms launched in 1963 by Mohammad Reza Shah of Iran and approved in a referendum. "White" meant bloodless, a revolution from above to head off a red one from below.

Its centre was land reform. Large estates owned by landlords, clergy endowments and the crown were bought up and sold on to the peasants who worked them. Other points included votes for women, the sale of state factories, profit sharing for workers and a literacy corps of young conscripts sent to teach in villages.

Many peasants got land, but plots were often too small to live on, and water rights and credit stayed hard to get. Millions moved to the cities, where they swelled the slums of Tehran. Landlords and the Shia clergy lost wealth and power.

The cleric Ruhollah Khomeini denounced the reforms, was arrested, and riots broke out in June 1963. He was exiled in 1964. The rural upheaval, oil wealth and the Shah's growing autocracy all fed into the Iranian Revolution of 1979. Compare the Green Revolution in farming of the same years.
sum: The White Revolution was a set of reforms launched in 1963 by Mohammad Reza Shah of Iran and approved in a referendum. "White" meant bloodless, a revolution from above to head off a red one from below.
